theme: La llamada de los discípulos — la red, el barco y el trabajo de la noche (Mateo 4:21; Lucas 5:5). Unidad de consolidación de A1.
storyThread: La llamada de los discípulos: junto al agua, dos hermanos y su padre en el barco, las redes que remendaban, la voz que llamó, la noche de trabajo sin pesca y la red que se echa a la palabra del Maestro. L1 = la llamada (llamó, red, barco, pescador, maestro, trabajó). L2 = lo que pasó después (escucharon, vas, cuestan, se levantan, tarde, a veces). L3 = el cuidado del cuerpo, repaso de U5 (almuerzo, nariz, medicina, fiebre, diente). L4 = el repaso de la historia — the five named re-passes (hermano, padre, noche, luego, camino).
grammarTargets: CONSOLIDATION UNIT — no new grammar. The two taught tenses meet in one pack: present (vas, cuestan, se levantan) and regular preterite (llamó, trabajó, escucharon); the tense contrast is tested in gap-fill with the written time marker (ayer / hoy), never by ear alone

the -ar preterite plural spine -aron is closed here (escucharon) after U7 opened it with llegaron; the person paradigm escucharon/escuchó NEVER shares a hear-choose set (C5/U5-7) and is resolved by the written subject in gap-fill (a1-u04 E6 precedent)
ir 2nd singular vas completes the paradigm a1-u03 left open (va/van) — the last open cell of A1's ir table
costar → cuestan completes the deferred E8 id; cuestan/cuesta is a person paradigm, never a shared hear-choose set
levantarse 3rd plural se levantan closes the U5-5 deferral; the reflexive pronoun stays attached to the tile (14 chars — LONG-tile debt)

IRREGULAR PRETERITES REMAIN UNBOUND AND UNUSED IN AUTHORED LINES: fue, dijo, vio, vino, tuvo, hizo, dio, pudo, estuvo, hubo, trajo + stem-changing 3rd persons → A2-U1. llamó/trabajó/escucharon are all REGULAR (B7)
no verse question is ever blind: Mateo 4:21 is HEARD and READ in its own block before any verse item is asked (owner quality bar 2026-11-11)
waveNotes: l1 (6) = the call: the two verse teaches-words (llamó mat-4-21, red lke-5-5) plus the story's nouns (barco, pescador, maestro) and the regular preterite trabajó. red/redes and trabajo/trabajó are the pack's two sharpest pairs, both documented. l2 (6) = what happened next: the -aron plural (escucharon), the two deferred paradigm cells (vas, cuestan), the deferred reflexive plural (se levantan) and two deferred time words (tarde, a veces). l3 (5) = the U5-5 deferred health/meal words, a body-care round that reuses U5's doler + definite-article pattern. l4 (5) = the FIVE NAMED RE-PASSES required by LEAD RULING R-4 (hermano, padre, noche, luego, camino) — all new:false with poolSource, glosses byte-identical, so the rebase chain can verify 399→416 exactly. tenemos is NOT among them: it landed at a1-u05 (C7 partially discharged there).

qna.nearFormRule: Never in the same hear-choose option set — INHERITED and still binding: cómo/como, vivo/vive, cree/crece/creó, por qué/porque, muro/pared, mi/mío, tu/tú, tiene/tienen, tienes/tiene, en/entre, nuevo/nuestro (a1-u02); va/van, ve/ven, ve/va, a/al, pueblo/puerta/puente, plaza/plato/planta, barro/burro, barro/carro, viaje/viejo, camello/camino, cruza/crece/cree, espera/escribe, cama/casa (a1-u03); mercader/mercado, esta/está, este/esta/esto/estos/estas, estos/estas, ese/esa, ese/este, camisa/cama, barato/barro, color/calor, verde/verano, rojo/ropa, cuesta/cuántos, cinturón/cintas (a1-u04); the levantarse paradigm, tengo/tenemos, me llamo/me lavo/me levanto, me visto/vestido, mano/mañana, mano/hermano, cara/casa, cara/cama, pierna/piedra, pie/pierna/piedra, siempre/nunca (a1-u05); padre/madre, the seven gender pairs, mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus, nuestro/nuestra/nuestros, mío/mi, tuyo/tu, suyo/su, primo/primero, abuelo/abrigo, tío/tiempo, generoso/gente, amable/amigo, vecino/verde (a1-u06). NEW IN THIS PACK: (1) THE PRETÉRITO ACCENT PAIR ora/oró — never a shared set; the tense contrast is tested in gap-fill with the written marker ayer (U7-2); (2) the LLEGAR PARADIGM llegué/llegaste/llegó/llegaron — never any two of them in one hear-choose set (C5/U5-7), tested in gap-fill with the written subject (U7-7); (3) lanza/lanzó (noun vs preterite, one character apart — the pack's sharpest pair); (4) salió/sal (prefix); (5) entró/entre and entonces/entró/entre (en- cluster); (6) escuchó/espera/escribe (es- cluster); (7) espada/espera (es- cluster); (8) llegó/lleva (lle- cluster); (9) león/lejos (le- cluster); (10) valle/calle (one-letter pair); (11) gigante/gente (g- cluster); (12) luego/hasta luego (superstring); (13) por fin/por qué/porque/por favor (por- cluster); (14) celebró/celoso (cel- cluster); (15) piedra/pierna (inherited). DOCUMENTED EXCEPTIONS (deliberate, kept): (a) ayer/hoy/mañana sit TOGETHER — the past/present/future frame is the teaching point; (b) subió/bajó sit together (hill/valley pair); (c) entró/salió and salió/volvió/entró sit together (the direction pairs); (d) escudo/espada/lanza sit together (the armory contrast); (e) después/primero/entonces/luego form the sequence set (a1-u05's order-pair exception, extended); (f) corazón/cabeza/cuerpo remain a1-u05's documented set and are also this pack's verse-complete options; (g) a1-u02's hay/está/tengo, mi/tu/su, cuántos/cuándo and a1-u04's demonstrative exceptions remain documented (none co-occur here). NOT IDS, therefore NEVER option strings (phantom decoy, DEFECTS #14): armadura, coraza, casco, batalla, monte, montes, fuerte, oso, campamento, suelo, frente, altura, soldado, filisteo, gigantes, hondo, abeja, calló, juego, caminó, and every present-tense partner listed in qna.charset. NEW IN THIS PACK (a1-u08, consolidation): (1) red/REDES — the verse's plural token is never an option string and never a tile (exact-string rule); (2) pescador/pescado/pescar — never a shared set (es- cluster); (3) maestro/mercado (inherited mercader/mercado family, extended); (4) trabajo/trabajó — the pack's own accent pair, never a shared hear-choose set (U8-4); (5) the -aron plural spine escucharon/escuchó — never a shared set (person paradigm, C5/U5-7); (6) vas/va/van and cuestan/cuesta — person paradigms, never shared sets (a1-u03/a1-u04 inherited); (7) se levantan/se levanta/me levanto — the levantarse paradigm, never a shared set (U5-7); (8) the three meals almuerzo/desayuno/cena sit together on purpose (documented exception, U8-5); (9) tarde/temprano sit together on purpose (the meaning is the contrast); (10) nariz/mano, diente/nariz, medicina/fiebre are a MEANING cluster, never a near-form pair; (11) diente/dientes and nariz/narices — the plurals are not ids.

qna.grammar: A1 register per THEOLOGY-guide §3.1: THE PAST IS NOW TAUGHT — pretérito of REGULAR verbs only (this is A1's one pretérito wave; the standing present-only rule is discharged for authored lines from here on). Present tense remains for nouns and markers. No subjunctive; affirmative familiar imperatives only (toca, señala). IRREGULAR PRETERITES ARE NOT USED IN ANY AUTHORED LINE: fue, dijo, vio, vino, tuvo, hizo, dio, pudo, estuvo, hubo, trajo, pidió, durmió, murió, sintió → A2-U1. Every say is one idea and the target word is repeated in caption + sign. Scripture is exempt from the tense rule (standing ruling) and 16:7 is present-tense anyway.
qna.csa: Clean. The call of the disciples, a night of work, a shared meal and ordinary illness/care. No threat imagery, no violence, no doctrine-assent gate (INT-1). The five re-passes carry their original glosses; the health words name care plainly (fiebre/medicina) and are never applied to the learner as a condition.
